about: ONE TABLE, READ BY ALL THREE. The planner reads the values and the stages from it at each plan, orrery bakes it in for the explanations and the queue's reasons, and the lab report draws its figures from it. A word changed here changes everywhere, so a screen and the report cannot tell two stories. Keep it to characters the console's fonts have (ASCII, and the arrow).

values.label: Ease now
values.what: How far every pass bar sits under z 3 right now. Held z = 3 less this. Changing it moves the bar once; each generation then takes the step below off it.
values.up: generations come sooner, more of them truly worse
values.down: generations come later, each worth more

values.label: Ease ceiling
values.what: The easiest a dry spell may make the bars. Past 2.75 the simulated gain a day falls away and half of what passes is truly worse.
values.up: a dry spell ends sooner, on noise
values.down: a dry spell lasts longer, and passes on evidence

values.label: Harder each generation
values.what: What each generation takes off the ease.
values.up: the bar climbs fast, then a dry spell brings it back
values.down: the bar stays put; 0 is a fixed bar

values.label: Dry before easing
values.what: How long with no generation before the bars ease. Paul set four hours.
values.up: the fleet waits longer on a hard bar
values.down: the bar gives up sooner

values.label: Easing step
values.what: What a dry spell adds to the ease, at once and again each interval below.
values.up: a dry spell ends in fewer steps
values.down: a dry spell ends gently

values.label: Easing again every
values.what: After the first easing, how long before the next.
values.up: slower to reach the ceiling
values.down: quicker to reach the ceiling

values.label: Read-on bars eased at most
values.what: How far the keep-reading bars may fall with the rest. Simulated, more than 0.5 buys no gain a day and spends lanes on what is dropped later.
values.up: more trials read on, fewer new trials
values.down: more new trials, each read less

values.label: Proof bar
values.what: How far past main the carried line must read to go on main. The ease is taken from this for a generation, and nothing is taken for main. Moving it also moves the generation bar.
values.up: main moves rarely and surely
values.down: main moves often, and a false line can reach players

values.label: Line against main every
values.what: How often the line gets its 800 seeds against main.
values.up: more lanes left for trials
values.down: main catches up sooner, at a cost in lanes

values.label: Anchor reads back
values.what: How many generations back each new generation is read against, to catch slow drift.
values.up: catches slower drift, on an older baseline
values.down: catches only recent drift

values.label: Queue depth a machine
values.what: How many jobs wait for each CPU machine. The queue is first come, so depth is how long a finding waits.
values.up: no lane starves between plans
values.down: a finding is read sooner

values.label: Passes carried a generation
values.what: How many trials that passed on the old defaults get one more read on the new ones when a generation lands. 0 throws them away, as it was.
values.up: fewer finds are lost, more lanes go to re-reads
values.down: more lanes go to new trials

values.label: Between generations
values.what: A generation does not land sooner than this after the last. What passes meanwhile waits and lands together. 0 lands each as it passes, as it was.
values.up: fewer reads overtaken, larger and less separately read batches
values.down: finds reach the line sooner, more reads lost to the generation after

values.label: Long reads, fast machines
values.what: Held-out reads and proofs go only to machines marked fast in config.json, 9 minutes against 41. 0 lets any machine take them. If none is fit, any does.
values.up: long reads finish sooner, builds reach slow machines sooner
values.down: more machines can take them when the fast ones are busy

values.label: The fit forgets at
values.what: An older read counts for less: its error grows by this many points for each doubling the defaults have moved since it was read.
values.up: the fit trusts today's reads more
values.down: the fit leans on what it read before

values.label: The fit looks back
values.what: A read is not used once the defaults have moved this far since it, a switch counting as one, and never across a game. 0 is today's reads alone, as it was.
values.up: more reads, older and less like today
values.down: fewer reads, each more like today

values.label: Looking far
values.what: Under each new game, every dial is read alone at a quarter and four times today's value, this share of each top-up until they are done.
values.up: the far read finishes sooner, fewer lanes for the fit
values.down: more lanes for the fit, a stale dial stands longer

values.label: Read the temperament
values.what: Every this many generations, each entry of the waves-to-temperament matrix is read each way alone, with three reads of 400 seeds to fold. 0 never.
values.up: fewer lanes spent, the matrix goes stale
values.down: the matrix follows the brain more closely

values.label: Temperament's share
values.what: How much of each top-up those trials may take until they are done.
values.up: a round finishes sooner
values.down: more lanes for the fit

values.label: How hard a wave
values.what: Each trial sets one entry to this, plus and minus: at the wave's peak the dial moves by this share.
values.up: easier to see, further from what a good setting is
values.down: closer to a usable setting, harder to see

values.label: Test the net's width
values.what: Every this many generations, counted from now, record new matches and train the same data at widths 32, 64 and 128. 0 never. It changes no net: past the bar it raises a flag for a person.
values.up: less machine time, a later warning
values.down: sooner told if the net has run out of room

values.label: Seeds to record for it
values.what: How much new data each width test records. bc2 was trained on 1,260. Too few favours the narrow net, since a wide one needs more to fit.
values.up: a fairer test of the wide net, hours more recording
values.down: a cheaper test that leans narrow

values.label: Bar to say widen
values.what: How much better 128 must agree than 64 on drive and gun, on held-out seeds, before it raises a flag for a person.
values.up: fewer false alarms, a later warning
values.down: sooner told, more often for nothing

values.label: Seeds in a held-out read
values.what: How many starting worlds a held-out read plays. The proof is two of them.
values.up: a read is surer and takes longer
values.down: a read is quicker and noisier

stages.title: Propose a trial
stages.input: the ledger of every census; RANGES; the defaults
stages.simulates: Nothing: this is arithmetic. suggest.py fits the ledger and draws from what it does not yet know; A/B flips each switch and each choice; wide trials look far from today.
stages.why: A trial is a question about one set of dials. Every later step only answers it, so better questions are cheaper than more seeds.
stages.adds: The source of every number the game's bots run on.
stages.queued: A new question: nothing else makes the search look anywhere new.

stages.title: First read, 55 seeds
stages.simulates: Bots only. Each seed is one starting world on one of eleven maps, played three times so that each team takes the trial seat once: 15 minutes of game time and three respawns, the trial brain against the baseline.
stages.why: The cheapest honest read. Half of all trials stop here, and that is what pays for the long reads.
stages.adds: Nothing yet: it spends lanes so the long reads go to what might be real.
stages.queued: First read: drops the hopeless for the price of 55 seeds.

stages.title: Read on, stage by stage
stages.simulates: The same census on fresh seeds. Reads pool by inverse variance, and a trial leaves as soon as its z says keep, drop or pass.
stages.why: A sequential test: seeds go where the answer is still open. Simulated, this read 40% more real finds a seed than a fixed count.
stages.adds: Nothing yet: it decides which few earn a held-out read.
stages.queued: Still undecided: more seeds settle it, and it holds no bar yet.

stages.title: Held-out read, 400 seeds
stages.input: a trial past the read-on bar
stages.simulates: The census on seeds no search has seen, from 60,000,000 up. Selection has picked out lucky first reads, and only unseen seeds can say so.
stages.why: This is the read that makes a generation. High priority: it decides, and it once waited seven hours behind what did not.
stages.adds: The evidence every generation's commit message carries.
stages.queued: Decides a generation: unseen seeds are the only fair read of a selected trial.

stages.title: Families hold their floors
stages.output: plan/families.json: pass or fail by family
stages.simulates: Set pieces, not whole matches: a raid on a guarded base, a dodge, a kite. Each scenario has a floor a brain must keep.
stages.why: An average can rise while a skill is lost. The families are what the census cannot see, and they caught it on 5899e8e.
stages.adds: Keeps the behaviours a person notices when the score alone would trade them away.
stages.queued: A candidate waits on this: it must not lose a skill the average hides.

stages.title: Tests, then the line
stages.simulates: No match: the brain's own unit tests on a branch. set-defaults.py rewrites the defaults, and if they pass the commit joins the local line.
stages.why: This turns numbers into code, and it is the only step that writes to treadcore. A test that pins a default it does not name stops the line here.
stages.adds: The generation itself: new defaults in the brain's source.
stages.queued: Writes the generation: tests on a branch, then the commit the fleet builds next.

stages.title: Every machine builds it
stages.output: census-bin at the commit, on each machine
stages.simulates: Nothing: a cargo build per machine. A read counts only on today's defaults and today's game, so this resets what is asked next.
stages.why: The next generation starts from this one. This is how weights are carried: the search never looks for them again.
stages.adds: Makes the new brain the baseline everything is read against.
stages.queued: The new generation's baseline: nothing can be read on it until this finishes.

stages.title: Anchor: back three
stages.input: the defaults of three generations ago
stages.output: a trial read as any other
stages.simulates: The census with the old values against today's. If the old read better, drift is undone by the same road a find takes.
stages.why: Generations pass at a low bar, so some are truly worse. This is the correction for what the ratchet lets through.
stages.queued: Catches drift: reads today against three generations back.

stages.title: The line against main
stages.output: 2 x 400 seeds: z of line over main
stages.simulates: The census with main's values against the line, on fresh seeds from 700,000,000 up. All the generations' noise is in one read and cannot pass it by luck.
stages.why: Generations are unproven on purpose. This is the single gate between a fast search and what players get.
stages.adds: Decides what reaches the game on origin/main.
stages.queued: The gate to main: nothing reaches a player until the line reads past it.

stages.title: Main: the game's brain
stages.simulates: Nothing: a push. Every machine fetches it, and a release carries it to players.
stages.why: This is where the fleet's work becomes the game.
stages.adds: All of it: Commander, tactics, crew and fleet read these defaults in every match.

stages.title: Transform: learned override
stages.input: the senses, the rules' answer, the biorhythm
stages.simulates: The same census with the patch switched on, SPSA moving all 942 numbers by one noisy read a step. All zeros is the brain as it was.
stages.why: The rules decide and a small net may move their answer if it is confident. This is the first learned part with a path to one brain.
stages.adds: The file style 5 ships. The search still will not promote one by itself.
stages.queued: Learned override: one more SPSA step on a net the rules can fall back from.

stages.title: The game reads a slot
stages.output: nets/patches/1.bin, in the game as style 5
stages.simulates: Nothing here: a file shipped in the binary. Under a census it is read from the queue, as before.
stages.why: Now a learned improvement can ship and a person can choose it. Off unless chosen.
stages.adds: Style 5, Overrider: the rules, with the transform moving their answer when it is sure.

stages.title: GPU islands: crucible
stages.input: champions from the other islands; the ladder
stages.simulates: Crucible's own arena on the card: 2,048 small nets duelling, 128 episodes, 100 generations a segment. Different physics, senses and net from the game.
stages.why: It is the only use of the GPUs, and it is very fast. It learns to duel, which is not yet the game.
stages.adds: Champions, which the bridge plays as style 7.
stages.queued: GPU search: keeps the island's population moving between exams.

stages.title: Bridge: crucible to treadcore
stages.output: nets/duelist.bin, in the game as style 7
stages.simulates: A real match: the champion's 35 inputs are built from what a tank sees, and its gate decides when it takes over the fight from the rules.
stages.why: This is what lets GPU work reach the game. An adapter, so it plays in a world it never trained in; a census says how it does.

stages.title: One brain, by name
stages.output: bot styles 0 to 7, chosen a team at a time
stages.simulates: A real match: any mix of rules, dials, transform, net and champion on one map.
stages.why: A person can now ask for a kind of mind by name.

methods.name: The dial search
methods.what: Fit, draw, read: suggest.py over the ledger, then the sequential census.
methods.gives: about 120 numbers in weights.rs and tactics.rs

methods.name: A/B versions
methods.what: Every switch flipped and every choice's other versions, each generation.
methods.gives: which functions run: 18 switches and each choice

methods.name: Families
methods.what: Set pieces with floors, for each candidate.
methods.reaches: the game, by what it refuses

methods.name: Anchors and the proof
methods.what: Today read against three back, and the line read against main.

methods.name: The transform (SPSA over 942)
methods.what: A residual net over the rules' answer, moved by one census a step.
methods.reaches: the game as style 5, chosen by a person

methods.name: Crucible's GPU islands
methods.what: Populations of nets duelling on the card, swapping champions.
methods.reaches: the game as style 7, chosen by a person

methods.name: Imitation: record, train, school, gauntlet
methods.what: Recorded matches teach a net to play as the rules do, then it is examined.
methods.gives: nets/bc2.bin, the learned tank, about 20 a seat under the rules
methods.reaches: the game as style 6, chosen by a person

methods.name: Whole-brain sweeps: switches, parts, census, round robin
methods.what: Each switch or part alone against the defaults.
methods.gives: a reading of what each part is worth
methods.reaches: people, and the fit through the ledger

methods.name: Older searches: SPSA and tune on dials
methods.what: Gradient and evolution over a chosen few dials, a run at a time.
methods.gives: trials, by way of the same census
methods.reaches: the game, had they found anything the fit did not

screens.does: Adds a computer to the fleet: probe it, apply a recipe, join it.
screens.ties: The very start of the line. No machine, no lane, no reads.
screens.drawn: A list with one step lit, because a setup is a sequence and the next step is what matters.
screens.look: A machine stuck on a step, or a recipe that says ready to run.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here. It only makes a machine able to run the census and build the brain.
screens.helps: More lanes means more seeds an hour, and that is the only currency the search spends.

screens.does: The cards and images the machines were made from.
screens.ties: Before the line: how a machine came to exist.
screens.drawn: A ledger of cards, because a card has no other record.
screens.look: A card whose image is older than the fleet's.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here.
screens.helps: Only indirectly: it lets a dead machine come back the same as it was.

screens.does: The fleet's disks and shares: survey, share, mount.
screens.ties: Where results and snapshots could live. The training record is stored apart, by fleet-archive.py.
screens.drawn: A patch bay, because a share is a connection between two machines.
screens.look: A disk filling up, or a 10 Gb link not plugged in.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here.
screens.helps: Indirectly: nothing learned is worth much if the record of it is lost.

screens.does: Says which machine works on what: treadcore or crucible.
screens.ties: Sets which lanes feed the dial track and which feed the GPU track.
screens.drawn: A grid of machines by projects, because that is the only question it answers.
screens.look: A machine on no project, or a project paused and forgotten.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here. It chooses who runs what.
screens.helps: Directly: CPU lanes on treadcore can reach the game, and GPU lanes on crucible cannot yet.

screens.does: Each machine, its job now, and its buttons.
screens.ties: Every stage of the line, seen by machine.
screens.drawn: A row a machine with a lamp, because the question is whether anything is idle.
screens.look: A lamp not lit under a full queue, or one machine on old work.
screens.sim: Whatever each machine shows: mostly the census, 15-minute matches of bots on eleven maps.
screens.helps: An idle lane is lost seeds. This is where you see that first.

screens.does: Asks for a one-off run, cancels one, accepts one.
screens.ties: A side door into the line: what a person asks goes before the standing search.
screens.drawn: A list by run, newest first, because a run is a thing someone asked for.
screens.look: A run failed or left running with no lanes.
screens.sim: Whatever the run is: a census, a sweep, a recording.
screens.helps: Only when a person has a question the search would not ask.

screens.does: The whole line as tasks: order, machines, expected time, and the next essential task.
screens.ties: This is the line. Each bar is a stage.
screens.drawn: A Gantt for order and time, and a Kanban for state. Arrows are dependencies, and the red box has most depending on it.
screens.look: Red: the biggest blocker. NOT BUILT: a gap in the road to one brain.
screens.sim: Nothing itself. It reports the medians the fleet measured in the last day.
screens.helps: It says which single thing would free the most work.

screens.does: How data moves: what each stage takes in and gives out, and one real trial traced through.
screens.ties: All of it, by the files that pass between stages.
screens.drawn: Boxes and arrows with the file named on each arrow, because the question is what connects to what.
screens.look: How far each trial got, and where the road stops: a red box means data goes no further.
screens.sim: Each box says what it simulates. Pick a trial below to see its reads.
screens.helps: It shows which work reaches treadcore and which does not yet.

screens.does: Every machine: what it did, what it does now, and what it will do next.
screens.ties: All stages, by when and by whom.
screens.drawn: A row a machine with now as a line: left is measured, right is a forecast from the medians. Colour is the stage.
screens.look: Gaps on the left are lost time. Green marks are generations. A lane of one colour shows where the fleet spends itself.
screens.sim: Bars are mostly the census. Crucible's arena on the -cuda rows.
screens.helps: It shows the shape of the spending, which is the easiest place to find waste.

screens.does: What is waiting and running, each with why it is there.
screens.ties: Each row names its stage in the line.
screens.drawn: A list in queue order, because that is the order things will happen.
screens.look: Priority work behind a long queue, or one kind crowding out the rest.
screens.sim: Each row says which: a census, a family, a build, the GPU arena.
screens.helps: It lets you judge whether the fleet is asking the right questions.

screens.does: The numbers that set how hard a generation is. Change them here and the next plan uses them.
screens.ties: The bars of Read on, Held-out and the Proof.
screens.drawn: One row a value with its default and range, so nothing can be set past what it was tried at.
screens.look: A value away from its default, and whether the generation gap on the Board answers.
screens.sim: Nothing itself. tools/plans/difficulty-sim.py simulates what a value buys.
screens.helps: Too easy and the line fills with noise. Too hard and nothing is carried.

screens.does: Trials past their held-out read: a list of what may become a generation.
screens.ties: Between Held-out and Tests.
screens.drawn: A filterable list, because the questions are which are current and which promoted.
screens.look: Current ones waiting, and the same one failing tests twice.
screens.sim: The rows are census reads. The seeds are unseen by the search.
screens.helps: These are the finds. Everything before exists to fill this page with few true ones.

screens.does: Each improvement read, by dial and by machine.
screens.ties: Search and First read: the ticker of what was tried.
screens.drawn: Rows by dial, because the fit learns by dial and you may want to see what it is learning.
screens.look: A dial that keeps coming up, or one machine reading differently from the others.
screens.sim: First reads: 55 seeds, 15-minute matches, on all eleven maps.
screens.helps: It is what the fit reads next. A machine reading oddly poisons it, as the Mac's one-map bug did.

screens.does: The learned tank's net: its weight matrices.
screens.ties: The imitation method, dormant since 30 October.
screens.drawn: Matrices as heat maps, since a net has no other shape to look at.
screens.look: Dead rows or columns: a sense or action nothing reaches.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here. Its training imitated recorded rule-brain matches.
screens.helps: It is the net the census can seat. No player meets it yet: the game's client does not load a net.

screens.does: What needs a person, and what progress was made.
screens.ties: Every stage can raise one.
screens.drawn: A list you can acknowledge, because a flag should be answered once.
screens.look: Red, unacknowledged; or the same flag rising again.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here.
screens.helps: It keeps the line automatic: the fleet asks only when it must.

screens.does: The brain as a patch: dials, switches and the transform, in order.
screens.ties: Search and Transform: where each number acts.
screens.drawn: A signal path, because the brain is rules, then dials, then an override.
screens.look: Stages at zero: they cost nothing and do nothing.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here. It maps what the census simulates.
screens.helps: It shows which stage of the brain a search can move.

screens.does: Each dataset's reads as a landscape over two dials, with its local maxima and what works on each.
screens.ties: Search: where the fleet has looked, and what it has not. Select a region to send it trials.
screens.drawn: A surface, because peaks read at a glance, and the same ground flat, because a region and a job can be placed there. Red flags have nothing on them.
screens.look: Places to look, never results. A peak on thin support is one lucky read, and 'read' means seeds stood there, not that it won.
screens.sim: Past censuses, moved to today's defaults by a small fit of the dials since moved. Only reads that moved one of the two dials count.
screens.helps: It shows whether every maximum in every dataset is being worked on, and asks for work on those that are not.

screens.does: How the GPU champions' nets change over time.
screens.ties: GPU islands.
screens.drawn: A spectrogram of singular values, because it shows a net's structure growing without reading weights.
screens.look: New bright rows: new directions. Flat means the island has stopped learning.
screens.sim: Crucible's arena, not the game.
screens.helps: It tells you whether GPU work is still moving, even before it can reach the brain.

screens.does: Tables of each layer of the shipped net.
screens.ties: The imitation method.
screens.drawn: Numbers for rank and norm, and a map from senses to outputs.
screens.look: Low stable rank: the net uses little of its size.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here.
screens.helps: It tells you how big a slot needs to be.

screens.does: Which senses the net listens to, drawn round the tank.
screens.ties: The imitation method, and the transform's inputs.
screens.drawn: A disc with forward at the top, since most senses are compass sectors.
screens.look: A dark channel: a sense nobody uses, and a candidate to remove.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here.
screens.helps: Fewer senses mean a faster census and a smaller transform.

screens.does: What tanks do at each wave's high against its low, and the matrix of how far waves move temperament.
screens.ties: Search: the census folds its behaviour over each seat's waves, and the matrix's dials go by the ordinary road.
screens.drawn: A grid, waves by behaviours, each cell the difference with its error, because three waves are three separate questions.
screens.look: The waves driving nothing first: that row is what chance looks like. A cell past two errors in the others, more than in that one.
screens.sim: Real matches, read from the census logs. It shows waves changing behaviour, and only a census says if it wins.
screens.helps: It says if a wave reaches a tank's behaviour at all before anything is built on it.

screens.does: The road from trial sources to main, with live counts.
screens.ties: All of the dial track.
screens.drawn: Boxes and arrows with counts. Pipeline/Flow is the fuller one, with files named.
screens.look: A count that stops rising.
screens.sim: It reports census counts.
screens.helps: A quick read of whether the road is moving.

screens.does: The room of machines: a live tile for each.
screens.ties: Beside the line: any machine, any time.
screens.drawn: Tiles, because a room is looked round, not read.
screens.look: A dark tile, or a machine hot under load.
screens.sim: What the screen shows, or a terminal.
screens.helps: Only when something is wrong and you need to see for yourself.

screens.does: Terminals for each machine, kept alive in tmux.
screens.ties: Beside the line: hands on a machine.
screens.drawn: A grid of terminals, for watching several things at once.
screens.look: A build error or a stack trace nothing reported.
screens.sim: Whatever you run.
screens.helps: It is how a person fixes what the keeper cannot.

screens.does: Who may command the fleet, what each machine is, and the verbs.
screens.ties: Beside the line: the authority over machines. Its certificate decides whether Orrery can reach them.
screens.drawn: Machines by question, because you select by what is true of them, then act.
screens.look: A certificate near expiry, or a machine answering differently.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here.
screens.helps: It keeps the machines up, updated and alike, so reads can be compared.

screens.does: One room to talk with each machine, kept on the machine.
screens.ties: Beside the line.
screens.drawn: A transcript, as a chat is.
screens.look: A machine that stopped answering.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here.
screens.helps: Not directly. It is for asking a machine a plain question.

screens.does: Is it running as it should: the keeper's checks, and its buttons.
screens.ties: Under the whole line.
screens.drawn: Checks with lamps, because the only question is what is amber or red.
screens.look: An amber or red lamp, above all search, difficulty and starving lanes.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here.
screens.helps: A keeper down means every lane stops within a job.

screens.does: The work that repeats over many generations: its options, and what it last found.
screens.ties: Search: looking far, remembering, the temperament matrix, the width test.
screens.drawn: Rows of options as on Values, with each watch's last result above them.
screens.look: A width test past its bar, and rounds that have stopped finishing. An option at 0 means that work is off.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here. A press is live at the next plan, about a minute.
screens.helps: Long jobs are set once and read from time to time, without being asked for again.

screens.does: The line the fleet builds, newest first, with the defaults each changed.
screens.ties: Tests, Build and Main: the generations themselves.
screens.drawn: A list by commit, because each generation is exactly one commit.
screens.look: How often a commit is a generation, and whether a machine is behind.
screens.sim: Nothing runs here. The census read each commit's values before it was written.
screens.helps: This is the brain's history, number by number.
